env.description:
Env binds the integration's declared environment variables for this
deployment, keyed by env var name. Each binding is either a literal value or a
reference to a cluster secret. HTTP_PORT/HTTP_HOST are orchestrator-managed and
cannot be bound here. Literal values are persisted as-is; secret bindings
persist only the secret name, never its value.

expose.description:
Expose opts the deployment into an external HTTP endpoint. "external"
publishes a {subdomain}.{baseDomain} Ingress with TLS; empty = internal only.

replicas.description:
Replicas is the desired runtime replica count; <1 is normalized to 1. The
per-deployment Service load-balances across them for internal callers.

slug.description:
Slug is the user-chosen internal address label for a networked deployment
(the internal Service is octo-int-{slug}). It must be unique across
deployments; empty asks the orchestrator to allocate a free one. Ignored for
integrations with no HTTP source. Input only — the resolved slug lives in
Metadata.

snapshotId.description:
SnapshotID is the version tag (snapshot) to deploy. When the service is wired
with a snapshot store (the production path) it is required, and the deploy
ships that snapshot's frozen definition rather than the live one. Input only —
the resolved snapshot id/tag are recorded in Metadata.

subdomain.description:
Subdomain is the external host label; empty defaults to the integration
slug. Only meaningful when Expose is "external".

tracing.description:
Tracing runs this deployment's pods with the runtime's tracer on, so every
flow, block and model call they execute is published for the platform to
store. It is off by default and costs throughput, so it is a per-deployment
switch rather than an integration-wide one: you turn it on for the deployment
you are investigating.

env.description:
Env are the deployment's persisted env bindings, so a rollout dialog can seed
"edit existing". Omitted when the deployment has no bindings.

tracing.description:
Tracing reports whether this deployment's pods run with the runtime tracer on,

info.description:
The control plane behind the Octo platform: integrations and their
resources, version tags, deployments, cluster secrets, the
deployment-scoped key-value store, users and API keys, and the
site-wide settings.

The orchestrator is an in-cluster service and performs no
authentication of its own. Callers reach it over the cluster network
and the platform BFF is the authorization boundary in front of it.
Identity, where a route needs it, is passed as a parameter (an actor
id, a user id in the path) rather than proven by a credential.
info.title: Octo Orchestrator API

post.description:
How a caller holding an octo API key is identified. An expired or unknown token is
a 401 rather than a 404, so an attacker cannot tell the two apart.

get.description:
Reads the db_version row the schema job seeds, and passes the stored JSON
through unmodified so a caller sees exactly what was written. Reports 503
rather than failing when no database is configured, so the difference
between "not wired" and "wired and broken" stays visible.

500.description: the row could not be read

delete.description:
Removes the workload and its addresses, and cleans up the deployment's stored
data. The integration and its version tags are untouched.

get.description:
The deployment-scoped store the runtime calls. Values are raw bytes, not JSON, and
the current version comes back in the X-Object-Version header. Keys in a secret
namespace are encrypted at rest and decrypted here.

put.description:
The body is the raw value, capped at 1 MiB. Optimistic concurrency is by header:
send X-Object-Version with the version you last read and the write is refused if
someone has written since; omit it to write unconditionally. The new version comes
back in the same header.

post.description:
A rolling update in place: the id, address, scale and exposure survive. Each of
env and tracing is preserve-if-absent, so a plain version bump keeps whatever the
deployment was running with. This is also the only way to switch tracing on or
off, because the runtime reads it at startup and so only new pods see the change.
A tag that adds or removes the integration's HTTP source is refused — that
changes the Service topology, which a rolling update cannot express.

post.description:
Runs a version tag as its own Kubernetes workload. The body is optional and
defaults to a single internal-only replica. A tag is required in production: the
deploy ships that tag's frozen definition, so later edits to the integration do
not disturb what is running. Declaring HTTP_PORT is what makes a deployment
networked and earns it a stable internal address.
